Script Library

Keep Python scripts with a form that operators fill in — write, test and publish them in a small in-browser editor; every run is sandboxed by a runner with no database access.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WherePlugin Studio (first level of the sidebar) → Apps → New app → Script, in every ADOM (URL /studio/; a script's editor is /studio/scripts/<id>)

What is it?#

ℹ️Note

Now part of Plugin Studio. The Script Library and the Python console share one page, Plugin Studio (first level of the sidebar). The Explorer on the left switches between the panes and opens any app — a script too — in its editor. The editor has a Console tab to try code against the fleet data without saving it in the script. The page opens for a holder of studio.script_library or studio.python_console; each pane still needs its own permission. Old /database/scripts/… addresses redirect to /studio/scripts/….

Plugin Studio was called Python Studio until 2026-10-22, and it accepts Python code only. The custom-view studio that had the name Plugin Studio is now Report Studio. What you publish here appears for operators under Global → Plugins (Global ADOM), one entry per plugin (Plugins).

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-23: every script is an app. New app in Plugin Studio asks for the type; Script creates the script and its app with the same id and opens this editor. The Scripts pane is gone: scripts are listed in Apps with the type Script, next to the flow apps, with the same actions — Disable / Enable, Download data, Reset, Delete (see Plugin Studio apps). A script made before gets its app the first time an author opens Plugin Studio. The code, the form, the versions and the audience stay here, on disk, for the sandbox runner, which never holds a database connection. A disabled script app is offered to nobody, runs nowhere (not even as a step of another app) and its saved schedules are skipped — not paused — until it is enabled again.

The Script Library keeps Python scripts that come with a form. An administrator writes and tests a script, defines the fields an operator fills in, and publishes a version. Operators run that published version with their own values. Every run executes in the same bubblewrap jail as integration hooks, launched by a separate runner that has no access to the SATOM database or its encryption key.

What does it do?#

  • A small project per script. main.py is what runs; other .py files are importable modules and text files (.json, .csv, .yaml, …) are data the script opens by relative path. Up to 64 files of 512 KiB each.
  • An editor with a file tree, line numbers, Tab / Shift+Tab indentation, auto-indent after :, Ctrl+S and Check syntax, which lists each error with its file and line. The editor also saves by itself about four seconds after you stop typing.
  • The Apps pane of Plugin Studio lists every script as an app of type Script (published version, status, audience, last change) with the row actions Edit, Disable / Enable, Download data (its run records, as a zip), Download the code, Reset (deletes its finished run records) and Delete (the script, its versions, saved runs, run records and credentials; never for a template from Examples). New app → Script creates one.
  • Upload and download. Upload a single file or a .zip of the project (a zip of one folder is unwrapped); it is loaded into the editor and saved at once, as a new version. Download the current state or any version as a zip.
  • Every edit is a new version. Each save, upload and restore — of a published script too — is kept automatically as vN with its code, form and settings (Versions & runs). The starter template is not a version, so the first save is v1. Saves by the same person within ten minutes are grouped into one version; a save that changes nothing adds nothing. The last 100 versions are kept, and the published one always is.
  • Compare versions. Pick any two in the Versions card and click Compare, or use a row's compare button (that version against the previous one): a line diff per file plus the settings that changed. View opens any version read-only.
  • A form designer with a live preview of what the operator sees. Field types: text, textarea, number, select, checkbox, password and the database fields: lookup (pick one row), lookup_multi (pick several) and dataset (the whole result goes to the script).
  • Database fields. A query built in the designer — a table, other tables combined with it (only related tables are offered, with the join explained, up to two joins away), columns, filters, order and a row limit — that SATOM runs read-only for the user's ADOMs and hands to the script as rows. The script never touches the database.
  • Test runs of the saved draft with values you type, showing the output, the result() document and every connection attempt.
  • Credentials a script needs (user + password, or a single value), kept only in the vault and read with secret("NAME").
  • Connections the script may call — Studio connections to an external API or PostgreSQL database, ticked under Settings → Connections and used with connection("id"). The runner makes the call with the connection's credential outside the sandbox; the script never holds it.
  • Publishing. Publish approves the latest version under its own number (what you saw as v7 is what operators run as v7): code, form, network, timeout and the list of credentials, frozen. Operators keep running the published version while you edit. Restore saves an old version's content as a new version; nothing is deleted.

Limits of a run#

satom-scripts.service carries cgroup limits — MemoryMax=1G, TasksMax=256, CPUQuota=200%, low CPU and I/O weights — and a private /tmp that is a 512 MB memory filesystem holding the run's work directory, so a script that allocates, forks or writes in a loop stops there instead of taking memory, processes or disk from the database and the web service. Inside the jail the root and /dev are read-only, a file is at most 256 MB and the output is read as it arrives. At most 50 runs wait in the queue; run records are kept 30 days. Raise the limits in a drop-in (systemctl edit satom-scripts.service) if a site needs more.

Scripts in app packages#

When a flow app that runs a script is exported as an app package, the script's published version (files and settings) travels with it, together with the HTTP connections the script calls; credential values never do. To be accepted by the importing server, a packaged script must run with network None, declare no credentials, not use secret or tcp from the SDK, not pass write=True, have no database fields (lookup, lookup_multi, dataset) and declare only HTTP connections that exist there or come in the package. On import a missing script is created and published as version 1 for Administrators only; one that already exists is kept as it is. See Scripts in app packages for the exact refusal messages.

Requirements#

  • bubblewrap installed on the node, from Settings → General → System packages or with the installer. Without it every run is refused, never run unconfined.
  • satom-scripts.path enabled on every node. The installer enables it, and an update enables it on nodes installed before it existed.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the library, edit, test, publish, delete studio.script_library

studio.script_library is admin-only; only the seeded admin profile holds it. Without it Plugin Studio shows no Apps pane (and no entry at all unless the profile holds studio.python_console), and every /studio/scripts/… route answers 403. Every save, upload, test, publish, restore and delete is written to the audit log.

How to use#

  1. Open Plugin Studio (first level of the sidebar), click New app, pick Script and create it: a name and an id (lowercase letters, digits, -, _; the id cannot change later).
  2. Write main.py. Read the form values from satom_script:

```python from satom_script import inputs, result, log, tcp

log("checking %s:%s" % (inputs["host"], inputs["port"])) result({"ok": True}) ```

  1. On Form, add one row per value the operator must give: variable name, label, type, required, default and help text. The preview is the exact form. For a value that should come from the SATOM database, choose the type lookup, lookup_multi or dataset and build its query in the Database query panel that opens under the row:
  2. Pick the Table (for example Appliances (fleet)).
  3. To mix in another table, pick it in Combine with a related table: the list holds only the tables related to the one you picked, with the join in words (each Server Policies row belongs to one Appliances…).
  4. Tick the columns you want, add Filters, an Order by and the Max rows (500 at most).
  5. For lookup and lookup_multi, choose the Value (what the script gets) and the Label (what the user sees).
  6. Click Preview rows to see what your ADOMs return right now.
  7. On Settings, set the description, the timeout (5–900 s), who may run it (Administrators only or Operators) and the network: None or Outbound. Declare the credentials it needs, Save, then set each value with Set value.
  8. On Test, fill in the values and click Save and run the draft.
  9. When it works, Publish. Operators run the published version only, from Scripts; editing the draft afterwards changes nothing for them until you publish again.

What the script receives#

  • inputs — a dictionary of the form values, keyed by field name. Numbers arrive as numbers, checkboxes as True/False. Only fields you defined reach the script: anything else a form submits is dropped. The values come on standard input, never as environment variables.
  • Database fields arrive as rows SATOM read when the run was queued, for the ADOMs of the person it runs for (the operator for Run now, the owner for a saved run). Columns are named table.column; values are text, empty for NULL:

python dev = inputs["device"] # lookup log(dev["label"], dev["row"]["appliances.host"]) for d in inputs["targets"]: # lookup_multi: a list of the same log(d["value"]) for row in inputs["inventory"]["rows"]: # dataset log(row["appliances.name"])

The form keeps only the chosen value. Its row is read again for every run, so a saved run never works on an old copy. - result(data) — one JSON document shown as the structured output of the run. It is not parsed out of what the script prints, so printing JSON cannot fake it. - log(msg) — a timestamped line in the output (print() works too). - secret(name) — a declared credential from the vault: secret("FGT_ADMIN")["password"] or secret("API_KEY")["value"]. Raises KeyError when it is not set. - tcp(host, port) — a TCP socket for SSH or other non-HTTP protocols, e.g. paramiko.SSHClient().connect(host, sock=tcp(host, 22), …). Only with Outbound network. - connection(id) — a declared connection: connection("crm").get("/tickets", params={"state": "open"}).json() (also post, put, patch, delete, with json= or data=), or connection("cmdb").query("SELECT … WHERE site = %(s)s", {"s": "zrh"})["rows"] on PostgreSQL (read-only unless write=True). Works whatever the network setting, reaches only that connection's base URL, raises ConnectionError with the reason when SATOM refuses or the call fails, and each call is a line in the run's connections log.

⚠️Warning

Password fields cannot have a default, and their values are masked in every run record: in the output, in result(), in dictionary keys and in the connection list. A queued run keeps the values in a private file on the node that queued it; the runner rewrites that file without them as soon as it starts the run.

Advanced#

Advanced How a run is contained

The web application never runs a script. Test (and, later, an operator's Run) writes a request into data/scripts/queue/; satom-scripts.path starts satom-scripts.service, which runs as the satom user with no environment file — no database URL, no encryption key — and with the script sources read-only. It claims the request (at most once), copies the frozen files into a fresh directory and runs main.py inside bubblewrap: private process, user, IPC and network namespaces; only the system libraries, the Python environment (read-only) and the run's own directory are visible. Up to 4 runs execute in parallel.

Advanced Credentials and the vault

Values live at <mount>/scripts/<script id>/<NAME> in the vault configured under Settings → Vault — never in the SATOM database or on the node's disk. The page reads only the KV metadata to show stored / not set. When a run is queued, SATOM asks the vault for a wrapped read of each declared credential (single use, 15 minutes) and puts only those tokens in the request. The runner, which has no vault login, unwraps them as the run starts. A token someone else used first, or one that expired, fails the run with could not be unwrapped. Deleting the script deletes its credentials.

Advanced Network

None gives the script no network at all: no proxy, tcp() raises this run has no network access. Outbound routes HTTP(S) through a proxy that requests, httpx and urllib pick up on their own, and tcp() through the same proxy. The proxy refuses this node — loopback and every address it owns — and link-local addresses, checking the connected socket rather than the name. Every attempt is listed in the run record.

Advanced High availability

Scripts, versions and run records live under data/scripts/ and replicate to the standby with the rest of data/. The queue and the claims do not: a run belongs to the node it was queued on.

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Cause / fix
Sandbox unavailable on this node bubblewrap is missing — install it from Settings → General → System packages.
A test stays queued satom-scripts.path is not enabled on this node: systemctl enable --now satom-scripts.path, or run satom execute reinstall units.
cannot publish: main.py line N A syntax error in the draft. Drafts with errors are saved, but cannot be published or test-run.
egress denied: loopback of this node The script tried to reach this node. Scripts may only reach other hosts.
credential X could not be unwrapped The run waited more than 15 minutes, or something else used its token first — investigate the latter.
this script uses credentials, which need a vault Configure the vault under Settings → Vault.
A field value is refused It does not match the field type (a number, one of the select options) or a required field is empty.
… belongs to no ADOM, and your profile is confined to some ADOMs The query reads a table with no ADOM (no product, device or appliance column). A profile confined to some ADOMs cannot read it; use a table tied to devices, or ask an unconfined administrator.
… is no longer available for your ADOMs The value saved in the form (or in a saved run) is not in the query's result any more: the row was deleted, a filter excludes it, or it belongs to an ADOM the person the run is for cannot see. Pick the value again.
refused: the query references a credential table Credential tables (users, API tokens, settings secrets…) are never readable from the database tools, lookups included.
a pick list cannot group or aggregate Totals belong in a dataset field; a lookup needs one row per choice.
